title: A Theory for Record Linkage
abstract: Develops a probabilistic decision framework for determining whether two records refer to the same underlying entity. Agreement and disagreement evidence over multiple fields is combined into match, nonmatch, and unresolved decisions while controlling linkage errors.
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

title: On optimum recognition error and reject tradeoff
abstract: Derives an optimal classification rule when a classifier may reject uncertain observations rather than force a decision. It characterizes the tradeoff between recognition error and rejection rate, providing a foundation for explicit uncertain or abstain states.

title: Probabilistic linkage of large public health data files
abstract: Applies probabilistic record linkage to large data files using field-level agreement evidence and estimated match and nonmatch probabilities. The method operationalizes evidence-based identity decisions when identifiers are imperfect or inconsistent.

title: Incremental clustering and dynamic information retrieval
abstract: Studies clustering when observations arrive dynamically and clusters must be maintained as new points are inserted. The work provides foundational algorithms for incremental cluster maintenance rather than assuming a static batch assignment.
venue: Proceedings of the 29th Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing

title: On-Line New Event Detection and Tracking
abstract: Studies online detection of previously unseen news events and subsequent tracking of those events as additional stories arrive. The formulation requires distinguishing continuation of a known event from creation of a new event in a stream.
venue: Proceedings of the 21st Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval

title: Cross-Document Event Coreference: Annotations, Experiments, and Observations
abstract: Introduces cross-document event coreference as the problem of identifying descriptions in different documents that refer to the same real-world event. It presents annotations and experiments that establish event identity across document boundaries as a distinct coreference problem.

title: First Story Detection In TDT Is Hard
abstract: Examines first-story detection in Topic Detection and Tracking, where an incoming story must be recognized as the first report of a new event rather than a continuation of an existing one. The study highlights the intrinsic difficulty of this online novelty decision.
venue: Proceedings of the Ninth International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management

title: Topic Detection and Tracking Evaluation Overview
abstract: Describes the evaluation framework for Topic Detection and Tracking, including topic tracking, link detection, topic detection, first-story detection, and story segmentation. These tasks provide early operational measures for deciding whether arriving news items continue an existing event or initiate a new one.
venue: Topic Detection and Tracking: Event-Based Information Organization

title: A Framework for Clustering Evolving Data Streams
abstract: Presents a framework for maintaining clustering information over evolving data streams using compact online summaries and later macro-clustering. It is a general streaming-clustering foundation for tracking cluster evolution, although its clusters are not inherently identity-labelled work matters.
venue: Proceedings of the 29th International Conference on Very Large Data Bases

title: New event detection and topic tracking in Turkish
abstract: Evaluates new-event detection and topic tracking in a news stream. Incoming documents are assessed for whether they describe a previously unseen event and, for known events, whether they belong to an existing tracked topic.
venue: Journal of the American Society for Information Science and Technology

title: Classification Methods with Reject Option Based on Convex Risk Minimization
abstract: Develops classification methods that may reject an observation when evidence is insufficient for a reliable label. Convex surrogate losses are used to learn the decision and rejection regions, with consistency and risk analysis.

title: On the Foundations of Noise-Free Selective Classification
abstract: Formalizes selective classification, where a predictor may abstain on some observations. It analyzes the relationship between coverage and prediction risk, providing a principled framework for controlling errors by leaving uncertain cases unresolved.

title: Joint Entity and Event Coreference Resolution across Documents
abstract: Presents a joint model for cross-document entity and event coreference. It iteratively constructs clusters and exploits dependencies between entity and event mentions, including predicate-argument relations, so evidence about one type can improve identity decisions about the other.
venue: Proceedings of the 2012 Joint Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing and Computational Natural Language Learning

title: Toward Open Set Recognition
abstract: Formalizes recognition when test observations may belong to classes that were not present during training. It introduces open-set risk and methods for limiting assignment of unknown observations to known classes, directly supporting a principled new-or-unknown decision.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

title: Using a sledgehammer to crack a nut? Lexical diversity and event coreference resolution
abstract: Examines how lexical diversity affects event coreference and argues that earlier data can make event identity artificially easy when documents within a topic predominantly describe one seminal event. It introduces additional texts containing different instances of similar event types, making false merges between related but distinct events more visible.
venue: Proceedings of the Ninth International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation

title: Incremental Entity Resolution from Linked Documents
abstract: Studies entity resolution when linked documents are added incrementally rather than processed once in a static batch. Inter-document references and attribute similarity are used so that only a limited affected subset needs to be reconsidered after new data arrives.

title: Incremental entity resolution on rules and data
abstract: Develops incremental entity-resolution techniques for settings where either data or matching logic changes. Previously materialized resolution results are reused to update match-based, distance-based, and pair-oriented resolutions without recomputing everything from scratch.

title: Cross-document Event Coreference Resolution based on Cross-media Features
abstract: Addresses cross-document event coreference in multimedia news by combining textual event information with visual evidence from news video keyframes. The work tests whether cross-media evidence can help distinguish mentions of the same real-world event from other event mentions.
venue: Proceedings of the 2015 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

title: Towards Open World Recognition
abstract: Extends open-set recognition to an open-world setting in which a system must detect unknown classes and later incorporate newly labelled classes. The formulation is relevant to incremental identity systems because it separates recognition of known identities from creation and subsequent learning of new identities.
venue: 2015 IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition

title: Autonomous data stream clustering implementing split-and-merge concepts – Towards a plug-and-play approach
abstract: Proposes an autonomous single-pass clustering method for evolving streams that can incrementally split and merge clusters as structure changes. The work is generic data-stream clustering, but its explicit birth, fusion, and separation mechanisms are relevant to maintaining evolving cluster identities.

title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Develops selective classifiers that abstain on difficult observations so prediction risk can be constrained while retaining as much coverage as possible. The approach provides a practical mechanism for refusing low-confidence identity assignments instead of forcing every item into an existing class.

title: Improved suffix blocking for record linkage and entity resolution
abstract: Develops improved suffix-based blocking methods for record linkage and entity resolution and considers incremental processing after records are inserted. The approach reduces the comparison space while preserving candidates needed to update identity clusters.

title: Revisiting Joint Modeling of Cross-document Entity and Event Coreference Resolution
abstract: Introduces a neural joint model for cross-document entity and event coreference. Mention representations combine lexical context with predicate-argument relationships, enabling entity and event identity decisions to reinforce one another across documents.
venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: An incremental graph-partitioning algorithm for entity resolution
abstract: Presents incremental graph partitioning for entity resolution when new references arrive and pairwise similarities may change. Unlike purely greedy attachment, the method can revisit previous decisions when new or contradictory evidence changes the consistency of existing clusters.

title: Incremental Multi-source Entity Resolution for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Studies incremental multi-source entity resolution as new source entities are added to existing clusters. It combines efficient assignment with repair operations that can correct erroneous prior clustering decisions and reduce dependence on insertion order.

title: Case notion discovery and recommendation: automated event log building on databases
authors: Wil M. P. van der Aalst
abstract: Addresses construction of process-event logs when an appropriate case notion is not already fixed. It generates candidate case notions, correlates events into traces under those notions, and ranks alternatives, making it relevant to inferring case identity from multi-attribute event data.

title: Generalizing Cross-Document Event Coreference Resolution Across Multiple Corpora
abstract: Systematically compares cross-document event-coreference methods across several corpora rather than evaluating only in-domain. It shows that cues important for event identity vary across datasets and that neural models may generalize inconsistently, highlighting the danger of transferring benchmark accuracy directly to a different communication domain.

title: WEC: Deriving a Large-scale Cross-document Event Coreference dataset from Wikipedia
abstract: Introduces a large-scale English cross-document event-coreference dataset derived from Wikipedia. Unlike datasets restricted to predefined topic clusters, it supports event-identity decisions over a broader document collection and provides a substantially larger training resource.
venue: Proceedings of the 2021 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies

title: Cross-document Event Identity via Dense Annotation
abstract: Focuses explicitly on cross-document event identity and densely annotates related document pairs. The study examines full identity and closely related quasi-identity cases, exposing ambiguities that sparse coreference annotation can miss.
venue: Proceedings of the 25th Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning

title: Machine Learning with a Reject Option: A survey
abstract: Surveys machine-learning methods that can reject predictions rather than always return a class. It distinguishes rejection caused by ambiguity from rejection caused by novelty and reviews architectures and evaluation approaches for predictive and rejective performance.

title: Cross-document Event Coreference Search: Task, Dataset and Modeling
abstract: Formulates event-coreference search: given an event mention, retrieve mentions elsewhere in a large collection that refer to the same event. The task moves beyond predefined document clusters and tests event identity in a retrieval-scale setting.
venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

title: Privacy preserved incremental record linkage
abstract: Develops privacy-preserving incremental record linkage for adding records to previously linked data. New records may attach to existing clusters or form new clusters when no satisfactory existing match is found, directly reflecting an incremental continue-versus-new decision.

title: FIRLA: a Fast Incremental Record Linkage Algorithm
abstract: Presents an incremental record-linkage algorithm that updates previously established clusters when new records arrive instead of repeating full batch linkage. The work primarily emphasizes computational efficiency while retaining the underlying identity-linkage operation.

title: Cross-Document Event Coreference Resolution on Discourse Structure
abstract: Uses discourse structure to improve cross-document event coreference. Rhetorical relations and structured paths between event mentions provide contextual evidence beyond local lexical similarity for deciding whether mentions denote the same event.
venue: Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

title: Optimal Strategies for Reject Option Classifiers
abstract: Analyzes optimal reject-option strategies under several formulations, including cost-based rejection and constraints on coverage or improvement. It shows how an uncertainty score can support principled acceptance and rejection decisions and characterizes the resulting risk-coverage behavior.

title: Event-Case Correlation for Process Mining using Probabilistic Optimization
abstract: Addresses event-to-case correlation when event records lack reliable case identifiers. It uses probabilistic optimization over event attributes, ordering information, and process constraints to infer which events belong to the same process case.

title: Synergetic Event Understanding: A Collaborative Approach to Cross-Document Event Coreference Resolution with Large Language Models
abstract: Combines large-language-model event understanding with a smaller trainable coreference model. Event summaries and structured insights generated by the larger model are used to improve cross-document decisions about whether event mentions refer to the same underlying event.
venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Improving cross-document event coreference resolution by discourse coherence and structure
abstract: Improves cross-document event coreference by constructing coherent cross-document discourse representations and exploiting their structure. The method uses broader discourse evidence to distinguish coreferent event mentions from merely related events.

title: Hypergraph convolutional networks with multi-ordering relations for cross-document event coreference resolution
abstract: Models cross-document event mentions and several relation types with a hypergraph and learns representations using hypergraph convolution. Pairwise evidence is then combined with clustering to resolve event-identity chains across documents.

title: Position-aware end-to-end cross-document event coreference resolution for Dutch
abstract: Presents an end-to-end cross-document event-coreference model for Dutch that incorporates positional knowledge and graph-based representations. The approach is designed to reduce common coreference-chain errors while resolving event mentions across documents.

title: Classification with reject option: Distribution-free error guarantees via conformal prediction
abstract: Uses conformal prediction to construct reject-option classifiers with distribution-free finite-sample error guarantees. The method provides a principled way to trade coverage for reliability when evidence is insufficient for a confident assignment.
